why: Holmes's system is a study-specific classification artifact for organizing instructional-television research, not a general theory of learning or a reusable educational research method.
This is a context-bound empirical equivalence claim about Army instruction delivered by television, not a reusable design recommendation or instructional pattern.

This is a medium-specific application of Cognitive Load Management: limiting viewing duration, daily exposure, and audience size is intended to manage processing demands, although the reported thresholds are context-bound.
The TV-series clips are a narrower, language-teaching use of short video prompts, so the study belongs on the canonical Video Prompts page rather than as a separate TV-series treatment.

rejected.verifier: It concerns video-based exposure for vocabulary retention, not the use of clips as prompts to launch attention, discussion, or analysis.
